assertions.name: component_acn_exceeds_genus_lower_bound
assertions.source: Consistency of the bracket: the realisation value must exceed the genus-derived lower bound, since the minimised topological value lies between them.

assertions.name: pair_and_component_objects_differ
assertions.source: The correction has teeth: the correctly-indexed component-vs-link object differs from the per-pair one by more than 1 crossing, so the earlier probe's number cannot be reinterpreted as the right quantity.

description: CORRECTION probe (beans qou-b5yi, qou-a9li). A close read of Komendarczyk eq. (43) and Khesin Thm 3.6 overturns two things this branch was building on. (1) The Freedman-He asymptotic crossing number in the LINK bound is ac(L_k, L) -- one component against the whole link, summed over n COMPONENTS -- so the per-pair object computed in em-linking-borromean-acn.witness.json is the wrong index and the wrong sum. (2) Eq. (43) carries (pi/16)^(1/4), a pure constant, and NO volume factor; the Vol^(-1/3) treated here as 'the Freedman-He template' is Khesin's SINGLE-knotted-torus bound, misapplied to a multi-component configuration. This probe computes the correctly-indexed object and records both corrections against work already committed on this branch.

correction_1_wrong_index.source: Komendarczyk, arXiv:0808.1533v1, eq. (43), p. 26: E_{3/2}(X) >= (pi/16)^(1/4) ( sum_{k=1..n} ac(L_k,L)|Flux(X_k)| ) min_k |Flux(X_k)|
correction_1_wrong_index.indexing: sum over n COMPONENTS, not n(n-1)/2 pairs; no pair-indexed ac(L_i,L_j) occurs in either source
correction_1_wrong_index.invalidates: em-linking-borromean-acn.witness.json: its ACN_pair (1.6426) and its 'total link' reading (3x that = 4.928) are both the wrong object. The malformed question was 'is the PAIR minimisation constrained by the third component?' -- there is no pair minimisation.
correction_1_wrong_index.also_settles: the (a)-vs-(b) question that motivated the read: (a) 'unconstrained pair minimisation, so the pair is an unlink and the infimum is 0' is REFUTED, but not because the minimisation is constrained-over-pairs -- because ac is not a pair quantity at all. Komendarczyk's genus is minimised over surfaces in R^3 minus the OTHER components, so Brunnian-ness does hold the value up, via a complement constraint on a single-component Seifert genus.

correction_2_no_volume_factor.where_vol_came_from: Khesin Thm 3.6, the SINGLE knotted torus bound: int_T |xi|^2 >= (16/(pi Vol(T)))^(1/3) |Flux|^2 (2 genus(K) - 1). Not the link bound.
correction_2_no_volume_factor.retracts: docs/audits/2026-08-01-em-linking-reads-round1.md round 4 claimed the empirical kappa ~ A^(-1/3) scaling had CONVERGED with an independent structural reason from Freedman-He, and that this raised it from 'unexplained fit' to 'candidate with a structural reason'. That is WRONG: the two routes were never independent, because the second was a misattribution. The claim is retracted.
correction_2_no_volume_factor.consequence: H_FH_A and H_FH_Z revert to BARE POWER LAWS with no literature backing -- precisely the bar the anti-fit discipline says they must clear and now do not. This does NOT make coth-saturation correct; it removes its rival's warrant. The residual-drift evidence (em-linking-residual-structure) already leaned the same way, independently.

corrected_object.definition: ACN(L_k, L) = sum_{j != k} ACN_pair(k,j); under the S_3 symmetry of the Borromean complement every pair integral is equal, so this is (n-1) * ACN_pair with n = 3.

bracket.reading: 2*genus_cx(L_k) - 1 <= ac(L_k,L) <= ACN(L_k,L)[realisation]. The realisation value bounds the minimised topological value from ABOVE; the genus estimate bounds it from below. The bracket is wide and is reported as a bracket, not collapsed to a number.

corrected_object.genus_step_is_my_inference: Komendarczyk bounds ac(L_k, L) below by the smallest genus among surfaces in R^3 minus the other components, with boundary L_k. For Borromean, L_k is null-homologous there (pairwise lk = 0) so a surface exists, while mu-bar_123 = 1 != 0 obstructs a genus-0 spanning disk, giving genus >= 1 and hence ac >= 1. NEITHER SOURCE COMPUTES THIS -- the obstruction step is my inference and is flagged as such.

what_eq43_actually_predicts.structure: with a fixed local Borromean configuration the topological factor sum_k ac(L_k,L) is A-INDEPENDENT, and there is no volume factor, so ALL A-dependence of kappa must be carried by the flux: E ~ ac * Flux^2.
what_eq43_actually_predicts.reading: kappa falls by 2.099 across the series, so saturating eq. (43) with a constant topological factor would require the per-component flux to fall by 1.449 over the same range. That is a specific, independently-derivable quantity -- it is NOT derived here, and nothing is wired. The point of reporting it is to make the size of the remaining obligation visible: the FH link bound does not explain kappa(A) by itself, it relocates the explanation into the flux.

data.residual_gap: Freedman-He, Ann. of Math. 134 (1991) 189-229 is not in the corpus or in library/ (201 PDFs scanned by title metadata, no match), so FH's own definition of the minimisation domain for ac(L_k, L) is not directly verified. Both corrections rest on Komendarczyk's statement of it, which is unambiguous on the per-component indexing and on the complement constraint, cross-checked against Khesin Rmk 3.5 and Thm 3.6. Acquiring FH 1991 would close this.
